title: Best Explainer Video Examples
summary: Watch 13 real Golpo Studio explainer videos for products, training, science and more. See why they work and learn how to create your own.
body_markdown:
A product demo shows work moving through Intake, Review, and Done. A blue bat locates a moth through echolocation. Colored sound waves explain noise-canceling headphones. These are three of the **13 real Golpo Studio videos** you can watch below, alongside examples for lessons, employee onboarding, small businesses, customer support, reports, and technical topics.


**Every video in this gallery was created with Golpo Studio.** We selected them to show how strong illustration, clear visual progression, and clear narration can make a product, process, or idea easier to understand. Each example includes the full video, its Studio style and runtime, and a practical lesson you can apply to your own project.


Want to make an explainer with this level of visual polish?[Explore Golpo Studio](https://video.golpoai.com/golpo-studio) , then use the creation walkthrough after the examples. You can also browse the[official Studio video library](https://video.golpoai.com/golpo-studio/videos) , where these examples are collected.

## 1. A demo that actually explains


Golpo Studio · Expressive Editorial Marker · 2:08


[Open the original video](https://golpo-ai-use-cases-long-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/03.mp4) .


This illustrative product story turns release information toward a practical question: what can the user do now? A colorful board uses Intake, Review, and Done to make a workflow visible. Arrows and marked items help explain movement through it. Later cards bring the communication back to one clear story.


**What makes it strong:** The viewer keeps recognizing the workflow as the explanation adds detail. That continuity is useful for product onboarding and process changes. This is an illustrated workflow example, rather than a recording of a named customer's application.


## 2. How bats navigate in darkness


Golpo Studio · Expressive Editorial Marker · 1:59


[Open the original video](https://whiteboard-video-library-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/topic-06.mp4) .


A blue bat, branches, and a moth establish a scene the viewer can recognize. Sound marks, an ear, and a delay-and-distance diagram make the invisible signal part of the picture. The explanation can develop inside a consistent visual world.


**What makes it strong:** The drawings connect an abstract process to visible objects and relationships. For your own educational explainer, choose the moment where an invisible cause needs to become visible, then give that moment enough space.


## 3. How sound-canceling headphones work


Golpo Studio · Bold Marker · 1:26


[Open the original video](https://whiteboard-video-library-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/topic-14.mp4) .


An ear and headphones give the mechanism a stable setting. A blue wave represents noise, while a red opposing wave represents anti-sound. The technical term arrives after the visual setup has given the viewer something to attach it to.


**What makes it strong:** Color carries meaning, and the main composition stays recognizable while the interaction unfolds. This is an especially useful approach for technical product explainers. Each color should keep the same job across your video.


## 4. A lesson students can see


Golpo Studio · Khan Academy Expressive — White · 2:23


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://golpo-ai-use-cases-long-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/01.mp4) .


This education example makes photosynthesis its central picture. A simple leaf gains sunlight, water and carbon-dioxide arrows, followed by oxygen and sugar labels. The explanation later moves closer to the leaf and adds a green internal structure, while retaining the same color cues for the inputs.


The useful creative decision is that the picture becomes more detailed as the idea develops. Viewers do not have to abandon one visual model and learn an unrelated diagram halfway through. Lesson-plan and notes illustrations also connect the finished video to the material a teacher already prepares, and a later comparison places a static diagram beside a video player.


**Best for:** teachers, course creators and EdTech teams explaining a process with identifiable inputs, outputs and stages. The same approach could suit a water cycle, a manufacturing sequence or an introductory biology concept.


**What to learn from it:** begin with a recognizable object, give each arrow a specific purpose, and add detail only when it helps the next explanation. For a classroom version, review the narration and diagram together against your lesson source before assigning it.


## 5. The first week at work


Golpo Studio · Bold Marker · 2:21


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://golpo-ai-use-cases-long-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/02.mp4) .


The opening pairs a thoughtful new employee with a large reference document. That document grows headings for Systems, Steps, Contacts and Security, while a separate first-step question makes the problem visible: having information does not automatically tell someone where to begin.


The video then gives practical questions their own space. A door introduces arrival, an inbox and report show reporting, and a branching line separates an IT access question from an operations task. The thick outlines and restrained blue, red and yellow accents make these categories easy to recognize. Near the end, a policy folder, checklist and video frame connect the explanation back to its underlying materials.


**Best for:** employee onboarding, internal process changes and training where people need to know the next action and the right contact.


**What to learn from it:** organize the video around the newcomer's questions. “Where do I begin?”, “What do I report?” and “Who can help?” produce a more useful sequence than reading a document's headings aloud. Replace the illustrative roles and steps with your organization's approved instructions before sharing your own version.


## 6. A small business, a clear story


Golpo Studio · Colorful Whiteboard Sketch · 2:06


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://golpo-ai-use-cases-long-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/04.mp4) .


A loaf of bread introduces this small-business story. The picture expands to a customer, a clock, a checklist and an empty basket, giving an everyday product a setting and a reason to matter. A delivery box and a basket of bread then make the offer concrete.


The warm paper background and yellow clothing, packaging and basket keep the look friendly and consistent. Later cards bring together the customer, baking and conversation, with a “Weekly” label connecting them. The closing composition returns to the customer and bread basket beside a short invitation to see the plans. The offer stays recognizable from setup to call to action.


**Best for:** small-business marketing, local services and recurring offers that benefit from a familiar customer situation.


**What to learn from it:** give the audience a person, a need and an understandable offer before asking for a click. Use a few recurring objects so the final action feels like the next step in the same story. For your own business, substitute real product details, approved branding and the exact action the landing page supports.


## 7. The support answer people will finish


Golpo Studio · Minimal Whiteboard Sketch · 2:01


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://golpo-ai-use-cases-long-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/07.mp4) .


A CSV file, an Import panel and a short help document establish a specific support task. The video narrows to a table with Name and Date columns, using Mia and Leo as example rows. It then enlarges the date field and adds an MM/DD annotation, making a small formatting detail visible enough to discuss.


Later, upload, connected fields and a confirmation check appear above a simple sequence line. The ending returns to the imported customer table with a green check. That return matters: viewers can recognize what success should look like after following the steps. The light sketch treatment keeps the attention on fields, rows and actions.


**Best for:** SaaS help centers, customer onboarding and recurring questions about imports, setup or formatting.


**What to learn from it:** choose one problem small enough to solve in a single sitting. Show the input, the point where someone might get stuck, and the expected result. When adapting this approach for a real application, check the current interface and date rules; an illustrative diagram should not quietly become an outdated product instruction.


## 8. From report to visual story


Golpo Studio · Hand-Drawn Data Notebook · 2:06


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://golpo-ai-use-cases-long-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/08.mp4) .


A professional holding a report opens this document-to-video example. The next composition connects the report to a video player while crossing out a person simply reading from a page. The difference is made visible: the task is to build an explanation from the report's findings.


A “Three Findings” heading introduces a map and a comparison chart. Burgundy accents mark important details against detailed black notebook-style drawing. Later, a percentage is challenged, measurement labels appear, and a review checklist connects the video to the original report through Claim, Label and Visual. The final revision imagery makes source checking part of the story itself.


**Best for:** research summaries, internal reports, consulting presentations and briefings that need an understandable visual structure.


**What to learn from it:** choose the findings that deserve explanation and select a useful visual for each. A location may need a map; a change may need a chart. Keep the original available for readers who need the full detail, and verify every label and quantity. Its visual detail comes from careful drawing and a clear sequence of ideas.


## 9. Why traffic jams form without a crash


Golpo Studio · Khan Academy Expressive — Black · 1:16


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://whiteboard-video-library-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/topic-01.mp4) .


A line of colorful cars moves across a black drawing surface. A cyan arrow establishes the direction of traffic, while a magenta arrow introduces a wave traveling the other way. Below the road, a spring-like drawing gives the viewer a second way to picture the same relationship. The cars remain in view, so the analogy has something concrete to connect to.


This is an excellent example of making a systems explanation visible. The lesson depends on understanding two kinds of movement, and the screen gives each its own color and direction. Later spacing marks and a small clock add detail without replacing the original road. The viewer can keep looking at the same situation as the explanation develops.


**What to borrow:** When two processes happen together, show them together and give each a consistent visual identity. Keep the original example beside an analogy so viewers can connect the two.


**Best for:** Transport education, classroom science, and explanations of queues, delays, or feedback. The creative strength is the relationship between the diagrams; use subject-matter review when adapting the underlying model to another system.


## 10. How GPS finds your location


Golpo Studio · Khan Academy Classic · 1:41


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://whiteboard-video-library-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/topic-02.mp4) .


A phone, a road, and two café storefronts provide a familiar starting point. Satellites appear above that everyday view, followed by clocks and bright signal lines. The drawing then expands into intersecting distance diagrams before returning to the phone. The video gives an ordinary interface a story about the invisible work behind it.


What makes the sequence compelling is the change in scale. The viewer begins with an object they recognize, travels into the mechanism, and comes back with a reason to understand the opening differently. White line drawings keep the scene readable, while selective blue and yellow marks draw attention to the relationships that matter.


**What to borrow:** Start with the experience your audience already knows. Reveal the hidden process in stages, then return to the original experience. That return can make the explanation feel complete without introducing another example.


**Best for:** Technology lessons, location-based services, technical onboarding, and products whose useful output hides a complicated process. Keep diagrams appropriate to the lesson; a simplified illustration should help explain the system without becoming a claim that every implementation works exactly as drawn.


## 11. How internet packets reach the right device


Golpo Studio · Bold Marker · 1:45


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://whiteboard-video-library-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/topic-04.mp4) .


A blue mountain-and-sun image begins on a phone. Small numbered cards carry pieces of that recognizable picture into a diagram of routers, connections, an application server, and a laptop. The picture itself gives the viewer something to follow as the network becomes more detailed. A separate monitor remains visible, helping frame the question of where the information should arrive.


The strongest creative choice is keeping the information recognizable throughout the journey. The numbered cards are easier to track than generic glowing dots. By the time the diagram adds branches and a return arrow, the audience already has a visual reference. Smaller book, envelope, and delivery-truck drawings provide further concrete comparisons.


**What to borrow:** Give the information in your process a visible form. Follow the same document, request, image, or order from its starting point to its destination. Keep its identifying details stable as the surrounding system grows.


**Best for:** Network education, software onboarding, and technical explanations of data moving between systems. Focus your version on the audience's central question and verify the technical details separately; the film's visual map is a teaching simplification.


## 12. How a stock exchange matches buyers and sellers


Golpo Studio · Hand-Drawn Data Notebook · 1:31


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://whiteboard-video-library-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/topic-09.mp4) .


The video starts with a buy button on a phone, then draws a path through a broker and several possible destinations. Its central diagram is an order book: turquoise bids sit opposite salmon-colored asks, while a yellow matching-engine box connects the book to a trade and settlement. A share card provides a recurring example as the diagram develops.


The notebook treatment works particularly well here. The subject contains categories, conditions, and a sequence, so a page-like composition gives those elements stable positions. A viewer can compare the two sides of the order book while following the transaction to the right. Color acts as a label, reducing the need to explain the layout again at each step.


**What to borrow:** Give each role a fixed place and each category a consistent color. Then show one specific item moving through the system. The viewer should be able to distinguish the participants before following their interaction.


**Best for:** Introductory market education, transaction workflows, and business processes with matching or approval steps. The share and prices are illustrative elements in the video, rather than current market information.


## 13. Why airplane wings generate lift


Golpo Studio · Classic Chalkboard · 1:21


[Watch the full Golpo Studio video](https://whiteboard-video-library-20261104.shramankar.chatgpt.site/videos/topic-10.mp4) .


A hand and an airplane introduce the subject before the drawing narrows to a wing cross-section. Cyan curves show airflow around the white outline. Yellow annotations and an upward lift arrow then give the diagram more meaning. Later, a downward weight arrow joins the composition, turning the wing into a place where the viewer can compare forces.


This example shows how a restrained visual style can still carry a technical explanation. The black background gives the lines contrast, and the small palette assigns different jobs to the wing, airflow, and force arrows. The video spends its visual detail on the mechanism rather than continually replacing the scene with another airplane picture.


**What to borrow:** Move from the familiar object to the part that needs explaining. Keep that part on screen while you add the relationships one by one. Reserve your strongest color for the idea viewers should notice next.


**Best for:** Engineering lessons, technical product education, and explanations of forces or flows. An uncluttered diagram is a powerful teaching choice; review the narration and scientific simplifications before using a generated explanation as lesson material.

## What makes an explainer video great?


A strong explainer has a specific audience, one main question, and a visible progression toward an answer. The opening gives someone a reason to care. The middle makes the mechanism or change understandable. The ending makes the takeaway or next action clear.


Use the screen for the parts that are difficult to explain with words alone. A drawing can show where something sits, what moves, how two things differ, or why a step changes the outcome. If the narration describes a relationship, make that relationship visible.


Consistency matters as much as visual richness. Reuse the same name, color, and shape for a recurring object. Keep important labels legible on the destination screen. Give a difficult diagram time to settle before introducing another one. Music and transitions should support that progression.


For a product video, distinguish an illustrated concept from a literal demonstration. Use a real screenshot or recording when the viewer needs to verify an actual interface. For a factual lesson, check the script and the visual explanation against the source. Beautiful animation earns its place when it makes the idea easier to understand.


## How to make a studio-quality explainer with Golpo Studio


Start at[Golpo Studio](https://video.golpoai.com/golpo-studio) , then open the creation screen. The[Studio walkthrough](https://video.golpoai.com/guide/golpo-ai-complete-tutorial#how-to-use-golpo-studio) shows the controls. Studio is available from Growth and on Pay As You Go; individual controls depend on the plan.


1. **Write the audience and outcome.** Decide who is watching and what they should understand or do afterward. Choose one central question.
2. **Supply the material.** Start from a prompt or source document. Use Script Mode when you have approved narration. If Golpo drafts the words, enable the script review step before rendering.
3. **Select Golpo Studio and preview a look.** Compare the available examples, then choose a treatment that fits the idea and audience.
4. **Set the applicable narration and video options.** Choose the duration, orientation, language, voice, and music available for your workflow. An Own Narration recording supplies its own spoken language and runtime.
5. **Generate, watch, and refine.** Check the opening, factual details, labels, visual progression, and final action. Review the finished video at the size your audience will watch it.


The following brief is an original starting point you can adapt. It is separate from the scripts used in the 13 sample videos.


### An original 60-second product explainer brief


**Script — the words the narrator speaks:**


> A customer asks for an update. The answer is buried across messages, notes, and a spreadsheet. ClearPath puts every request on one shared board. New work enters Intake. The right person moves it into Review. Completed work reaches Done. Everyone can see the owner, the next step, and what is waiting. Instead of asking three people for a status update, your team can open the board and see the same picture. Start with one recurring request, agree on its stages, and try the workflow together. One visible process gives the team a clearer way to move work forward.


ClearPath is an invented product for this original writing example. Replace it and its behavior with your real product facts. Check the spoken runtime before choosing your final duration.


**Video Instructions — what to draw, where your plan includes this control:**


> Begin with scattered request cards. Bring them onto one clean board labeled Intake, Review, and Done. Follow the same blue request card through the three stages. Keep labels short and large. End on the complete board with one clear next step. Use original editorial marker artwork and purposeful motion.


**Voice Instructions — how the narrator should sound, where available:**


> Warm, confident, and conversational. Pause briefly when introducing each stage. Give the final action a clear, unhurried finish.


Keep those fields separate: Script supplies the spoken words; Video Instructions direct the picture; Voice Instructions shape delivery. See the[Video Instructions guide](https://video.golpoai.com/guide/golpo-video-instructions-power) and[Voice Instructions guide](https://video.golpoai.com/guide/golpo-voice-instructions-power) .


## What does a Golpo Studio explainer cost per minute?


Golpo Studio uses **one dashboard credit per 30 seconds** , or **two credits per minute** . At the standard Growth monthly price of $199.99 for 150 credits, allocating the whole allowance to Studio generation represents 75 minutes: $199.99 ÷ 75 = **about $2.67 per generated minute** .[Current pricing](https://video.golpoai.com/pricing) ,[credit rules](https://video.golpoai.com/guide/golpo-credit-deduction-guide) .


That calculation assumes full use of the allowance for Studio generation. Paid revisions, other credit use, unused allowance, add-ons, and your review time affect the cost of approved output. Canvas and Sketch use a different generation rate, so choose the engine before calculating your budget. For a deeper comparison, read[the explainer video cost guide](https://video.golpoai.com/guide/explainer-video-cost) .


## Frequently asked questions


### What is an explainer video?


An explainer video helps an audience understand a product, process, service, or idea through coordinated narration and visuals. The strongest examples use the screen to show relationships, changes, and steps that would be harder to follow through words alone.


### Were all these explainer video examples made with Golpo?


Yes. All 13 featured videos were created with Golpo Studio and are available through the official Golpo Studio library. Each example on this page includes a full video, a direct watch link, its visual style, and its runtime.


### What are some of the best Golpo explainer video examples?


Start with the product workflow, bat echolocation, and sound-canceling headphone videos. Then compare the training, support, report, traffic, GPS, network, exchange, and aviation examples. They demonstrate different ways to explain a task, a sequence, an invisible process, or a system.


### Can I create studio-quality explainer videos with AI?


Yes. The videos above show the animated explanations you can create with Golpo Studio. Start with your own topic, source material, or approved narration, choose a suitable style, then review and refine the generated result.[Open Golpo Studio](https://video.golpoai.com/golpo-studio) .


### How do I choose the right Studio style?


Look at the job the picture needs to do. A clear marker treatment can suit a short process. A notebook treatment can help organize data. An expressive illustrated scene can make a natural or technical mechanism memorable. Preview several looks and choose the one that keeps your own explanation easy to follow.


### How long should my explainer video be?


Use the time needed to answer one useful question. The examples above have different runtimes because they explain different things. Plan a complete progression from problem to mechanism to takeaway, then remove material that does not help the audience follow it.


### What should I check before publishing my explainer?


Watch the entire video. Confirm the product facts or subject matter, pronunciation, label accuracy, visual continuity, and final action. Test readability on the intended screen and confirm you have the rights to inserted assets and recordings.
